elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 retained sentence: "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims," and the operative cap opens "each Party's total aggregate liability."

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 as rendered: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Lower-case "fees" plus "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" displaces the illusory § 1.5 "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form); basis, lookback anchor (preceding the claim) and floor all match.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.2 retained verbatim: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims (outside the § 21.1 cap): "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations."

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is within Excluded Claims, and § 21.1 caps only "[e]xcept for Excluded Claims."
§ 21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed as an Excluded Claim.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property."

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: As rendered, § 21.3 carves out only "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services under this Agreement and any Order Form." The retained "undisputed" and "for conforming Services" limiters mean payment obligations as a whole are not excluded: disputed amounts later found owed, amounts referable to non-conforming Services, and other payment obligations (taxes, expenses, interest, reimbursements) remain inside the cap. The deterministic check on this carve-out also fails, and substantively the subset problem survives the change of basis from "Fees" to "amounts due."

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual."

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 as rendered measures the cap by "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim," with a USD 1,000,000 floor; the illusory single-Order-Form/Implementation-Fee basis is removed.
§ 21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations," which sit outside the § 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations."

reasons: Preferred level is one element short: the § 21.3 payment carve-out still reaches only "undisputed amounts due for conforming Services," so Customer's payment obligations as a whole are not removed from capped damages. To reach preferred, redraft that sentence to read substantially: "Customer's obligations to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form are not damages and are not subject to the limitation in Section 21.1," rather than qualifying by "undisputed" and "for conforming Services."

Fallback is fully met: the cap is expressly mutual, is now measured by twelve months of fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), and indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct sit outside the cap via the retained Excluded Claims definition. The redline is therefore position-complete at the fallback level and clears the walk-away line created by the illusory "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) basis.

Minimality holds: only the § 21.1 cap basis and the § 21.3 payment basis were touched; the mutuality sentence, the mutual § 21.2 exclusion (including the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence) and the full Excluded Claims list are retained verbatim, and no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned (§§ 1.5-1.6 remain in force for other uses), no cross-reference dangles, and no retained sentence contradicts the new cap; the lower-case "fees ... under this Agreement and all Order Forms" is model language and deliberately avoids the narrow capitalised "Fees" definition. Consider adding "(whether or not capitalised, calculated without reference to the definition of 'Fees' in Section 1.5)" only if the counterparty resists the ordinary-meaning reading.
